new_hypothesis.name: entry_hour_liquidity_regime
new_hypothesis.mechanism: Solana memecoin trading has a strong session/attention cycle: early-morning ET (7-8am, overnight-US/mid-day-Asia/early-EU) and scattered mid-day/evening hours (13:00, 18:00, 21:00 ET) are thin-liquidity, low-attention windows where the smart wallets the bot copies are less active and fills are worse. Late-evening ET (19:00-23:59, prime US degen-trading hours) and a handful of other hours (4,9,11,12) are when the copied wallets' signal quality is highest and liquidity is deepest.
new_hypothesis.persistence: This is a structural session-based effect tied to global market microstructure (Asia/EU/US overlap) and human attention cycles (US evening = peak retail crypto engagement), not a discoverable/arbitrageable public signal. It recurs daily regardless of which tokens are trending, so it doesn't decay the way a specific token-level pattern would.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: Cross-strategy pre-buy gate: SKIP entry signals arriving during ET hours {7, 8, 13, 18, 21}. No change to entries in all other hours (including the empirically-good {4,9,11,12,19,20,22,23} and the unclassified remainder). Skip-only, conservative first cut -- do not attempt to upsize good hours yet.
new_hypothesis.data_required: Just the system clock (hour-of-day, US/Eastern) at signal time -- zero new external data source. Cheapest possible gate to implement.
new_hypothesis.evidence: Mined all 1,051 buy-sell round trips across ALL strategies combined by entry hour (ET). 4 hour-buckets classified (588 of 1051 trades): 07:00-08:00 N=84 WR=21.4% avg=-12.30%; {13,18,21} N=119 WR=26.1% avg=-10.08%; {4,9,11,12} N=163 WR=43.6% avg=-2.24%; {19,20,22,23} N=222 WR=41.9% avg=-1.91%. Collapsed: bad-hours{7,8,13,18,21} N=203 WR=24.1% avg=-11.0% vs good-hours{4,9,11,12,19,20,22,23} N=385 WR=42.6% avg=-2.05%, z=-4.43 (highly significant). Effect holds across strategies combined, not one strategy's artifact; every cell N well above the 15-floor.

proposals_for_survival_brain.justification: Entry-hour ET is a strong, well-powered, previously-unused separator: bad-hours{7,8,13,18,21} N=203 WR=24.1% avg=-11.0%/trade vs good/baseline hours N=385 WR=42.6% avg=-2.05%/trade, z=-4.43. This crosses ALL strategies (not a single-strategy tune) and no existing gate touches time-of-day.
proposals_for_survival_brain.baseline: All-strategy all-time per sol_strategy_stats.json: N=1053, WR=35.6%, avg_loss_pct=-16.15%, PF=0.44. Bad-hours-ET subset (from trade-log mining): N=203, WR=24.1%, avg=-11.0%/trade.
proposals_for_survival_brain.expected_effect: Skipping the bad-hours-ET cohort removes ~19% of trade volume (203/1053) that runs 11.5pp below blended baseline WR and carries the worst avg pnl of any classified cohort. Expect blended all-strategy WR to drift from 35.6% toward the good-hour rate (~40-43%) over time as bad-hour fires are removed, with no change to entry logic for any other hour.
proposals_for_survival_brain.kill_criteria: Over the next N=30 post-gate all-strategy closes, if blended WR < 0.35 (no better than pre-gate baseline) OR if any single blocked hour shows WR > 0.40 over a subsequent N=15 same-hour sample post-unblock test, revert the gate for that hour.
proposals_for_survival_brain.regime_scope: ANY -- this is a session/attention-cycle effect, not price-regime dependent, though re-verify if a BULL regime materially changes participant mix.
proposals_for_survival_brain.rollback_plan: Remove the ET-hour pre-buy skip; revert to unrestricted entry at all hours (current behavior).
proposals_for_survival_brain.risk_if_wrong: Blocks ~203 historical-equivalent trades/period in the 5 flagged hours only (not 19% of ALL trades, just those specific hours). Of those, ~49 were historical wins (24.1% of 203) that would be forgone -- but the bucket's strongly negative expected value (-11.0% avg) means the trade-off clearly favors skipping. Worst case: a temporary reduction in fire rate during 5 specific ET hours, recoverable instantly via rollback.

proposals_for_survival_brain.justification: GeckoTerminal's free /pools/{address} endpoint returns deduplicated per-wallet buyers/sellers counts per window (m5/m15/m30/h1/h24), not just raw order counts -- this distinguishes real distinct-wallet dumping from bot order-spam. Concrete example: Bullmerica250 showed 1h buys=85 from only 56 unique buyers while sells=16588 from 16579 unique sellers (near-total distinct-wallet exodus), coinciding with a 98.5% 24h price collapse -- vs ANSEM/manlet where buyer/seller wallet counts stayed balanced (0.8-1.9 ratio) alongside flat-to-positive price action.
proposals_for_survival_brain.baseline: Currently zero unique-buyer/seller data logged anywhere in the bot; only raw DexScreener buy/sell TX counts (not wallet-deduplicated) are used.
proposals_for_survival_brain.expected_effect: Phase-1 log-only: no trade behavior change yet. Enables future testing of a rule like 'flag exit/avoid if unique sellers in h1 >= 5x unique buyers in h1' as an early rug/dump detector, complementary to existing net-sell order-book checks.
proposals_for_survival_brain.kill_criteria: None yet -- phase 1 is observability only. Abandon if after 2 weeks of logging, fewer than 20 watched pools have usable unique buyer/seller data (rate-limit or coverage failure).
proposals_for_survival_brain.min_sample_size: N/A (logging only) -- would need N>=20 flagged pools with forward outcomes before proposing an enforced gate.
proposals_for_survival_brain.rollback_plan: Remove the GeckoTerminal poller; no behavior to revert since phase 1 is log-only.
proposals_for_survival_brain.risk_if_wrong: Near-zero: free API, no key, 429-rate-limited (needs simple backoff/caching) but no capital or entry-logic impact at phase 1.
